summary: Backend-only testing of the new admin Marketing endpoints (share-event, stats, settings). Created /app/backend/tests/test_marketing.py with 18 pytest cases covering auth gating, valid/invalid channels, stats increment, settings persistence, and Pydantic validation. All 18 tests pass against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL using cookie-based admin auth.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/admin/marketing/stats uses a 7-day rolling window via week_start = now - 7 days, but the field name 'this_week' implies a calendar week (Mon-Sun). Consider clarifying naming or computing from start-of-week to match user expectation.
marketing_shares records do not store the admin user id; if multi-admin support is added later, attribution will be lost. Consider stamping request.state.admin into the document.

save_marketing_settings uses singleton _id='singleton' (string) which is fine, but get_marketing_settings projects {_id: 0} once and then re-builds the dict manually right after — the manual rebuild is dead-code-ish duplication. Could be simplified to `return {**MarketingSettings().dict(), **doc}`.

MarketingShareEvent.channel uses a free-form str + manual whitelist check; using Literal['native','facebook','copy','download'] would let Pydantic reject invalid channels with 422 automatically and document the contract (currently invalid channel returns 400 from manual check, missing channel returns 422 from Pydantic — inconsistent).
test_credentials: Admin: lrobe / L1964c10$ via POST /api/admin/login (httpOnly admin_session cookie)
seed_data_creation: Tests insert marketing_shares rows for each valid channel and write/restore marketing_settings singleton. Settings are reset to defaults at end of save test. Share events are not deleted (intentional — they only contribute to counters, no user-visible state).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Marketing endpoints fully covered in test_marketing.py with 18 cases. Auth gating uses module-scoped session fixture. To re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_marketing.py -v. BASE_URL is auto-loaded from /app/frontend/.env if env var unset. No frontend testing performed (per request).
